Regulation: B.C. Reg. 133/2026
Made under: Environmental Assessment Act
Published in: No. 14 – B.C. Regs. 125 to 148, July 28, 2026
Deposit date: July 20, 2026

B.C. Reg. 133/2026, deposited July 20, 2026, under theENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT ACT[section 7]. Order in Council 349/2026, approved and ordered July 20, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that the attached Required Consent (Simpcw First Nation – Reviewable Mine Projects) Regulation is made. — T. DAVIDSON,Minister of Environment and Parks; J. WHITESIDE,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. REQUIRED CONSENT (SIMPCW FIRST NATION –REVIEWABLE MINE PROJECTS) REGULATION 1In this regulation,"consent agreement"means the agreement between the government and the Simpcw First Nation titled "Consent Decision-Making Agreement for Mine Projects", negotiated and entered into under section 7 (1) (b) of theDeclaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Actand dated July 15, 2026. 2For the purposes of section 7 (b) (ii)[required consent]of theEnvironmental Assessment Act, the consent agreement is prescribed as it relates to the Yellowhead Copper Project. minutes_briefs.title: Mine projects in Simpcw First Nation territory now need the Nation's consent under a new BC regulation
minutes_briefs.summary: BC has made a regulation under the Environmental Assessment Act that requires the consent of the Simpcw First Nation before certain mine projects can go ahead. The regulation points to a 'consent agreement' (a formal deal between the province and the Nation, signed July 15, 2026, called the 'Consent Decision-Making Agreement for Mine Projects'). The regulation specifically applies this consent requirement to the Yellowhead Copper Project.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you are involved with the Yellowhead Copper Project or any reviewable mine project in Simpcw First Nation territory, confirm with the BC Environmental Assessment Office whether the Simpcw First Nation's consent is now required before you proceed.
